question.text: The line passing through the extremity $A$ of the major axis and extremity $B$ of the minor axis of the ellipse $x^2+9 y^2=9$ meets its auxiliary circle at the point $M$. Then, the area of the triangle with vertices at $A, M$ and the origin $O$ is

solution.text:
Equation of auxiliary circle is $$ x^2+y^2=9 $$ Equation of $A M$ is $\frac{x}{3}+\frac{y}{1}=1$
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get Coordinates of $M=\left(-\frac{12}{5}, \frac{9}{5}\right)$ Now, area of $\triangle A O M=\frac{1}{2} \times O A \times M N$ $=\frac{27}{10}$ sq units
